source.title: Transformers Linearly Represent Highly Structured World Models

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether neurons can have specific, interpretable roles using activation analysis and causal ablation in a Sudoku transformer, rather than auditing neuron poles with the original explanation-and-testing procedure.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own measurements of final-MLP neuron specificity and causal effects. These bear on the qualitative one-neuron/one-job idea in V1, but it does not estimate the share of all neuron poles with one job. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reverse-engineers a small 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku traces. It picks out 91 final-MLP neurons with an activation-gap cutoff and shows they are monosemantic naked-single detectors. It does not estimate what share of neurons (or neuron poles) have one job, does not study Qwen3-32B or any language model, and does not test explanations on held-out text or simulate activations. Showing that a selected subset is monosemantic does not bear on any version's proportions or claims. Its only population-level remark is that most cell–neuron gaps cluster near zero, which concerns this one feature, not interpretability of the rest. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right but incomplete. The authors also conclude that the model builds a substructure-level (row, column, box) linear world model rather than a per-cell one. They further find that mid-layer attention heads act as substructure-specific constraint checkers. The naked-single circuit is their third result; they limit all findings to one architecture and one puzzle type.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes neuron activations, logit contributions, and causal ablations in a Sudoku-solving transformer; it does not use the neuron-pole explanation and held-out explanation-testing audit described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The detector set depends on an activation-gap cutoff of 3.0; the study does not report results across alternative cutoffs.

fits_no_version.finding: In a Sudoku-trained 8-layer transformer, 91 final-MLP neurons, selected by an activation-gap cutoff, fire only for their cell's naked-single state. They cover all cells with naked singles and their ablation has a cell-specific causal effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small transformers trained on structured reasoning tasks contain sparse, monosemantic, causally cell-specific neuron circuits for task decisions.

record.problems: Only one 8-layer model trained on one puzzle type is studied. The 91 neurons are selected using a stated cutoff, and the study does not estimate the share of all neurons or poles with one job. The authors also note that results are limited to a single architecture and task.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B, no neuron poles, and no share of neurons with one job, two jobs or not yet understood.
No language models, scale comparison, or dense vs mixture-of-experts comparison.
No InceptionV1 or reanalysis of a canonical polysemantic neuron.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools.
No neuron-based attribution graphs in a large model and no comparison with replacement models.
No test of whether explanations predict firing beyond activating examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the rows to V1 and labelled it supports. That link is wrong: V1 is an audit share in Qwen3-32B, and a cutoff-selected set of 91 monosemantic neurons in a toy Sudoku model cannot bear on that share. The study does not cite the essay or OpenAI's automated-explanation work. I chose relation 'discusses' and tranche T6 because the study addresses neuron monosemanticity generally without testing or using the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B, neuron poles, the proportions with one or two jobs or not understood, or test explanations on held-out activating examples.
No comparison across models, architectures, or scales.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 or the cat-and-car example.
Does not compare architectures, regularization, tools, or interpretability estimates across vision models.
Does not build attribution graphs or assess reconstruction error in a large language model.
Does not test explanations against activating examples or measure whether they predict firing.
Does not score automated neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku solving traces
rows.operation_detail: Selected final-MLP neurons by the gap between mean activation for exactly one candidate and the maximum mean activation for other candidate counts; cutoff 3.0.

conditions.value: naked-single state for a specific cell

rows.measure: Number and specificity of naked-single detector neurons
rows.baseline: Maximum mean activation across other candidate counts used in the activation-gap definition
rows.value: 91 neurons; the study reports that they fire exclusively for their associated cell's naked-single state and remain unactivated otherwise.
rows.note: This is a selected detector subset, not an estimate of the fraction of all neurons or neuron poles with one job.
rows.check: The value comes from selection: 91 neurons chosen by a cutoff of 3.0. It shows monosemantic detectors exist in a Sudoku transformer, not the share of neurons or poles with one job in a language model.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku solving traces
rows.operation_detail: Counted associated naked-single neurons per cell.
rows.measure: Coverage and number of associated neurons per cell
rows.value: 71 cells have a single associated neuron and 10 cells have two; coverage is complete.
rows.note: The reported cell counts describe the identified detector set, not all neurons in the layer.
rows.check: Describes how the selected detector set covers cells, not interpretability across all neurons; the subject is not a language model.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku solving traces
rows.operation_detail: Projected identified neurons' output weights through the unembedding matrix to measure their logit contribution when firing.

conditions.value: placement tokens for the associated cell

rows.measure: Mean logit contribution to the associated cell's placement tokens
rows.value: +3.00 logit boost on average; σ = 0.10 across the 9 target digits.
rows.note: The contribution is associated with the cell, rather than selecting the digit; the paper says the boost is essentially digit-uniform.
rows.check: Logit contribution of the selected neurons; does not measure any version's quantity.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku solving traces
rows.operation_detail: Projected identified neurons' output weights through the unembedding matrix to measure contribution to other empty cells.

conditions.value: placement tokens for other empty cells

rows.measure: Mean logit contribution to other empty cells' placement tokens
rows.note: Control for whether the identified neurons' contribution extends beyond their associated cell.
rows.check: Control for the selected neurons' specificity; not linked to any version.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku solving traces
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablated the neuron or neurons associated with the cell the model was about to predict.

conditions.value: 1,000 held-out states with two simultaneous naked singles

rows.measure: Change in target placement logit and softmax probability; table reports clean minus ablated scores
rows.note: The paper reports that the clean run splits probability roughly evenly between the two naked-single placements.
rows.check: Causal ablation of the selected neurons; shows their role, not a population share.

rows.subject: 8-layer transformer trained on Sudoku solving traces
rows.operation_detail: In the same two-naked-single states, ablated the neuron or neurons for one cell and measured the other cell's placement.

conditions.value: 1,000 held-out states with two simultaneous naked singles

rows.measure: Change in other placement's logit; table reports clean minus ablated scores
rows.note: The study describes the effect on the other naked-single cell as barely affecting it.
rows.check: Within-puzzle control: the other cell's logit rises slightly (0.655). Not linked to any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Identified naked-single detector neurons in the Sudoku model's final MLP layer
reader_labels.reason: The selected neurons are reported to activate specifically for a cell's naked-single state, contribute to that cell's placement logits, and have a cell-specific causal effect (R1–R6). This supports the qualitative possibility of neuron-specific jobs, not the claimed audit proportions.
